links.outcome: under-triage rate of risk calibration in French and Arabic
links.effect: Multilingual adaptation model reached 0.994 under-triage in French and Arabic under language-asymmetric risk supervision; re-adaptation with language-invariant labels reduced it to 0.572 and 0.558.
links.quote: A multilingual adaptation model reaches 0.994 under-triage in French and Arabic under language-asymmetric risk supervision.

links.outcome: cross-form consistency across paraphrases varying in register, layperson and emotional framing
links.effect: Aggregate accuracy and consistency can conceal safety-relevant failures across communicative forms; no specific consistency numbers given in the abstract.
links.quote: Results reveal that aggregate accuracy and consistency can conceal safety-relevant failures.

unlisted_practices: Adapting models with source-derived, language-invariant risk labels instead of language-asymmetric supervision to reduce multilingual under-triage
Testing clarification-seeking behavior on deliberately under-specified inputs

screen.reason: The study develops and tests an evaluation benchmark (HerHealthEval) assessing multilingual and register-sensitive understanding/safety failures (such as under-triage and clarification behavior) of LLMs in women's health communication.
